content: Have you ever wondered where the water in our rivers comes from? Imagine a tiny, crystal clear drop of water starting its journey high up in the cold, snowy mountains. By the time it reaches the sea, it looks completely different. What happens to it on the way?
Think about it: If a river starts clean and blue in the mountains, why does the water look brown, grey, or even smell bad when it passes through a city?

content.title: The River's Journey
content.description: Watch how the river flows from the mountains, past villages, through cities, and finally into the sea. Notice how factories and city drains change the color of the water.

content: As the river flows, it passes through villages, towns, and cities. People use river water for bathing, washing clothes, and bathing animals. Factories release harmful chemicals into the water. This makes the water dirty and unsafe to drink. We call this Water Pollution.

definition: The contamination of water bodies (like rivers, lakes, and oceans) usually as a result of human activities.

question: Which of these activities makes the river water dirty?
options: Washing clothes and animals in the river

content: Reflection: Imagine you live next to a river. If everyone in your town threw their garbage into it, where would you get your drinking water from? Discuss with your friends.

Connection: In older times, ancient Indian cities like the Harappan Civilization were built near rivers like the Sindhu (Indus). Rivers are called 'Lokmata' (Mother of the World) because they give life. But today, our modern cities are slowly destroying these same rivers.

Mastery Challenge: Create a simple 'River Map' on a piece of paper. Draw a mountain, a river, a village, and a city. Mark the places where the river is clean with a blue star, and where it gets dirty with a red cross.
Have you ever made Nimbu Paani (Lemonade)? You add sugar and salt to the water, stir it, and suddenly... they disappear! Where did they go? Did they do magic?
If you mix sand in water and stir it, will the sand disappear just like the sugar did? Why or why not?

content.title: Dissolving in Water
content.description: Watch what happens when we drop sugar in one glass and sand in another glass. The sugar particles spread out and become invisible, but the sand sinks to the bottom.

content: Things that completely mix in water and 'disappear' are called Soluble. Things that do not mix, even after stirring, are called Insoluble. Some things dissolve, and some things change the colour of water (like turmeric or haldi).

definition: Substances that can dissolve in a liquid, like sugar in water.
Substances that cannot dissolve in a liquid, like sand or stones in water.

question: Which of the following things will NOT dissolve in water?

content: Reflection: Just because water looks clean, does it mean it is safe to drink? Think about salt water from the ocean. It looks clean, but it has too much dissolved salt!
Mistake: Thinking that clear water is always clean and safe to drink. Truth: Even clear water can have harmful germs or dissolved chemicals that we cannot see!

Connection: In science, water is known as a 'Universal Solvent' because it can dissolve more substances than any other liquid. This is why rivers easily get polluted—they dissolve the chemicals from factories!
Mastery Challenge: Take 3 glasses of water. In glass 1, mix some mud. In glass 2, mix a spoonful of milk. In glass 3, mix salt. Write down your observations for each glass in your notebook.
Imagine you are very thirsty, but the only water you have is slightly muddy river water. Would you drink it straight away? How can we make it safe to drink?
If we leave the muddy water in a bucket for a few hours without touching it, what do you think will happen to the mud?

content.title: Cleaning Water
content.description: Boiling water kills the germs. Filtering removes the dirt. See how bubbles rise when water boils, destroying invisible harmful germs.

content: There are different ways to clean water. We can 'Boil' it to kill germs. We can 'Filter' it to remove dirt. The best way to make water safe for drinking is boiling it.

definition: Heating a liquid until it bubbles and turns into vapor. Boiling water kills harmful germs.

content: Explain to students that modern homes have water purifiers (like RO filters), which do the job of filtering and killing germs automatically.

question: What is the best way to clean water and make it safe for drinking?

content: Reflection: Water is precious. When we leave the tap running while brushing our teeth, we are wasting water that has gone through a long journey and cleaning process to reach our homes.
Connection: In our society, getting clean drinking water is not easy for everyone. In many villages, women still walk for miles every day just to fetch a pot of safe drinking water.
Mastery Challenge: Be a Water Detective in your house! Check all the taps. Are any taps leaking? Measure how many buckets of water your family uses in a day for bathing and washing.
